name: EASY
blurb: Start here. Sparse boards that grow a little each time, so you can learn how the numbers add up before anything gets crowded.

name: NORMAL
blurb: The classic game: five tiers on a 30x16 board. Creatures pack in tighter for five boards, then the board itself starts to grow.

name: HUGE
blurb: Nine tiers on a huge board, with 30 HP falling to 24. The top tier is only one to three creatures, and you reach max level just in time to face them.

name: EXTREME
blurb: Strong creatures are as common as weak ones, so no number is safe to assume. Boards pack tighter and HP falls from 10 to 8.

name: HUGE x EXTREME
blurb: The hardest ladder: HUGE's nine tiers, EXTREME's flat spread, and 10 HP. By the end, every level-up past the first needs every creature below it cleared.

name: BLIND
blurb: No fighting: 1 HP, and any creature ends the board. Win by uncovering every empty cell. Tiers rise from five to seven.

name: HUGE x BLIND
blurb: BLIND on the largest boards in the game: nine tiers, 1 HP, no fighting. A test of endurance.

name: WRAPAROUND
blurb: NORMAL's boards with every edge joined - off the right is the left, off the top is the bottom. There are no edges or corners to work in from.

name: WRAPPED CROSS
blurb: A cross with opposite arm tips joined, turning four dead ends into two loops - stuck at one end, work in from the other. Reveal and Census available.

name: CROSS
blurb: Four narrow arms around a hub. Each arm is nearly all edge and plays like its own small puzzle. Reveal and Census available.

name: DIAMOND
blurb: A diamond-shaped board. Its stepped edges give you more edge cells to read from than a straight rim. Reveal and Census available.

name: DONUT
blurb: A ring with a hole in the middle, so there are two rims to work in from. Reveal and Census available.

name: RAGGED CAVE
blurb: Tunnels and caverns, a different cave every seed. Almost every cell is near an edge, so it reads easily and is packed denser for it. Reveal and Census available.

name: PYRAMID
blurb: A stepped pyramid, a cell wider on each side every row down. The bottom two rows start face   up: their empty ground open, and every creature there shown with its tier, waiting for you.   Reveal and Census available.

name: GEAR
blurb: A gear: eight teeth round the rim and a hole through the middle, so there are edges to read   from outside and in. Reveal and Census available.

name: CARD
blurb: A playing card, the size of four ordinary boards, with its four suits cut out where a Four's   pips sit. Every hole is another edge to read from. Reveal and Census available.

name: VALENTINES
blurb: A heart-shaped board: two rounded lobes over a long taper to the point. Reveal and Census   available.

name: STAR
blurb: A five-pointed star. Each point narrows to a single cell, all edge, and they meet round a   pentagon in the middle. Reveal and Census available.

name: ARCANE
blurb: Magic arrives. Earn mana by exploring and fighting, then spend it on Reveal and Census when deduction runs out. Boards run denser to match.

name: WORKOUT
blurb: NORMAL's boards with deeper level gates and one spell: Exercise, which fights your next battle a level higher and pays double EXP if you win. It starts at 30 mana and costs 10 more each cast; every level-up takes 10 back off.

name: ORACLE
blurb: Six tiers, all equally common, and only 8 HP falling to 6. Every spell is on offer - Census, Reveal, Exercise and Beacon - and you will need them.

name: DUNGEON
blurb: Rooms joined by one-cell hallways, new every seed. You may only act within two steps of ground you have uncovered. Hallways and doorways are always empty; the creatures are all in the rooms. Reveal, Census and Exercise available.

name: HIVE
blurb: Hexagons: six neighbours instead of eight. Numbers run lower and blank areas open wider, so the boards are packed denser to make up for it.

name: PAIRS
blurb: Every creature touches exactly one other creature, and no two pairs touch. A beaten creature's number is its partner's tier, and once both halves are found the ground around them is safe. Boards grow rather than crowd.

name: DOMINOES
blurb: PAIRS dealt as a double-six domino set: every pairing of tiers 1-6 appears once per set, so every tier is equally common. Later boards deal more sets, packed tighter.

name: PACKS
axis: Packs of one of every tier
blurb: Creatures travel in packs of six - one of every tier, all touching - and no two packs touch. Whatever a pack has not shown yet is all that can hide beside it; a complete pack is ringed by empty ground.

name: CHECKERBOARD
blurb: Even tiers stand only on light squares, odd tiers only on dark; empty ground can be anywhere. Light neighbours always add up to an even number, so whether a number is odd or even is decided by its dark neighbours alone.

name: CONGA LINE
axis: Lines of one of every tier
blurb: Creatures dance in lines of six - one of every tier, stepping up, down, left or right, never bunched into a 2x2 - and the tier 6 always leads. No two lines touch. A line can only carry on from its ends, so the ground around a half-found line is mostly empty.

name: SUDOKU
blurb: A 9x9 board where tiers 0-8 follow Sudoku's rules: each appears once per row, column and 3x3 box. The nine empty cells start open, some tiers are given in gold, and every board can be solved without guessing.

name: ULTRA HIVE
blurb: HIVE's hexagons, on a board that is itself a hexagon: six straight edges to read in from, and   every number still the sum of six neighbours at most.

name: PETRI DISH
blurb: A round dish that starts with its three largest blank areas open. You may only open a cell   touching ground you have uncovered, or touching a mark you have made beside it, so each   colony grows from its edge.

name: PATROL
blurb: Every creature walks a square beat, a cell per move, clockwise from its top-left corner: a   tier 3 walks three cells a side. Every click, sweep or wait is a move. A creature on ground   you have uncovered shows as a ?, and a mark draws a creature's whole route.
